statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail 7 (low) with Nasdaq-100 futures inside the CME weekend halt, against Stress 50 (elevated) from an unresolved Strait of Hormuz and a ten-year Treasury yield near a twenty-year high.
recommendation: Tail remains far below the 25 blocking threshold in every assessed hour, so the mapped policy state is EA_ON across the whole window. No danger window is published, because a market that does not trade cannot supply the observed price-path evidence a narrow evidence-based window requires. The CME reopen at 22:00Z on Sunday falls six hours beyond the end of this forecast.
headline: Weekend halt holds Tail at 7 while a rejected Hormuz deal and a fresh Houthi intercept keep Stress at 50
body: Nasdaq-100 index futures have been halted since Friday 21:00 UTC and do not reopen until 22:00 UTC on Sunday, six hours past the 16:00 UTC end of this forecast window, so every one of the twenty-four assessed hours sits inside a closed market. That remains the single most important fact for Tail, because the pathological price path Tail measures requires a tradable tape and none exists in this window. Friday's cash session closed constructively and without pathological structure. NDX finished at 30,608.14, up 0.42% or 129.28 points from a 30,478.86 previous close, inside a 30,413.59-30,667.56 range and roughly 0.5% below its 30,770.63 fifty-two-week high. The S&P 500 added 0.51% to 7,743.41, the Dow rose 0.93% to 51,828.62 and the Nasdaq Composite 0.48% to 27,068.72, capping a week in which the index gained roughly 2% on renewed tech optimism led by Meta's Muse assistant. VIX fell 5.11% to 14.87, near the low of its 14.68-15.94 daily range. The macro backdrop is the main source of Stress rather than Tail. The Federal Reserve H.15 release puts the two-year Treasury yield at 4.87%, the five-year at 5.03%, the ten-year at 5.18% and the thirty-year at 5.47%, with the ten-year close to a twenty-year high, against an effective fed funds rate of 3.88%. Under the risk contract that combination compresses multiples and raises the difficulty of the environment without itself denying mean reversion, so it belongs in Stress and Confidence rather than in Tail. The geopolitical picture advanced during this clock hour's news cycle. Speaking before formally rejecting Iran's proposal, President Trump posted an image relabelling the Strait of Hormuz, then dismissed the seven-day reopening offer with the statement that the deal would not be acceptable, and separately argued that Iran had outsmarted itself by closing the waterway and now had no money coming in. Iran's proposal, presented through mediators around the United Nations General Assembly, had sought a ceasefire including Lebanon, removal of the naval blockade, easing of oil sanctions and release of frozen assets, with President Pezeshkian offering nuclear inspections. Revolutionary Guard spokesperson Brigadier General Hossein Mohebbi responded that Tehran will not stop punishing the United States until Iran's seven conditions are met. Three escalation items are new since the previous assessment and belong in the record. Saudi air defences intercepted a Houthi ballistic missile aimed at Khamis Mushait, with two drones reported intercepted separately and no Houthi claim yet issued; United States fighter aircraft launched from the USS George Washington in regional waters; and the national average gasoline price has reached 4.49 dollars a gallon against 4.10 a month earlier, with strait traffic still running roughly 75% below pre-conflict levels. Against that, the White House reports positive and constructive conversations with mediators, and crude eased into the weekend rather than spiking, with WTI settling at 92.41 dollars, down 2.33%, and Brent also lower on the session. An unresolved waterway with softer crude and a two-sided diplomatic track is weekend gap risk and elevated Stress, not evidence of an imminent pathological price path. The shared Finviz context read this run is both stale and partial and was therefore not used as current evidence: its generated timestamp of 13:24:56Z is roughly 190 minutes old against the 90-minute freshness limit, and its futures and economic-calendar sections were unavailable. No delayed cross-asset futures read is claimed here, and its latest-session breadth and megacap sections carry no source as-of and cannot establish current NQ structure. Tail is therefore held in a 7-9 band across the window, with the rise from Sunday representing accumulated unpriced weekend headline risk ahead of the reopen rather than observed structure, and it never approaches the 25 blocking threshold. Stress runs 48-53, easing slightly through Saturday evening as the news cycle thins, then rising into Sunday as the reopen and a heavy macro week approach: Dallas Fed Manufacturing and a Barkin speech on Monday, JOLTS and consumer confidence on Tuesday, final second-quarter GDP with the August PCE price index on Wednesday alongside Micron's fiscal fourth-quarter results after the close, ISM Manufacturing and jobless claims on Thursday, and September payrolls on Friday. Confidence is 83 and decays to 74 across the window. Verified current levels, official yields, crude, volatility, a seven-day calendar and first-hand geopolitical reporting from within this clock hour are all in hand; what cannot be held, structurally rather than through thin research, is a live price path, and that is what caps Confidence while futures are closed. No danger window is published, because a narrow evidence-based window cannot be justified inside a market that does not trade.

After Friday's 21:00Z futures settlement Tail decayed from 12 to 7 and Stress eased from 50 into the mid-40s as the session's directional question closed out, with the mode shifting to normal. Stress has since drifted back to 49 through Saturday as the Hormuz rejection was confirmed, while Confidence fell from 88 to 82 as the last live observation aged.
outlookSummary: Every one of the twenty-four forecast hours falls inside the CME weekend halt, which runs until 22:00 UTC on Sunday, six hours past the 16:00Z end of this window, so no hour can contain observed price-path structure. Tail is held in a 7-9 band throughout; the rise from 00:00Z on Sunday is accumulated unpriced gap risk ahead of the reopen, not observed one-way structure, and it stays far below the 25 blocking threshold. Stress runs 48-53, easing through Saturday evening as the news cycle thins, then rising into Sunday as the reopen approaches with the waterway question left open by a confirmed rejection, a fresh Houthi launch intercepted over Saudi Arabia and a heavy macro week beginning Monday. The mode is normal while the halt dominates and turns mixed from 09:00Z on Sunday, when two-sided reopen risk becomes the defining hour-specific factor. Confidence decays from 83 to 74 purely through evidence ageing, since no live tape can refresh it. Mapped policy state remains EA_ON in every hour.
